note: Matches on starting point, fails on willingness to pay, and cannot be assessed on occupation. Neglected health holds squarely: he built roughly 30 lb of muscle under a trainer and lost all of it over four years, by his own account 'through work and stress and all those other things'. Good to great holds — he is not in crisis, trains four times a week already, and frames the goal as finding 'that right balance of what's realistic for long-term mobility and strength'. Not deconditioned holds on both halves: he is lean with a fast metabolism, has a home training space, and runs his own rotation of kettlebell, bodyweight and free-weight work. Income is the clear miss, and unusually it is self-declared before anything was presented: 'I would have liked to spend closer to $200 or $300 a month', which the rep immediately read as putting four figures out of range. He also cut his previous trainer as an expense during the pandemic. 'Successful' is deliberately recorded in neither list — occupation was never asked, and all the transcript offers is a Zoom display name associating him with Choose Chicago and a reference to having changed roles for his career, which is not enough to test the criterion either way. Two observations. First, this is the fourth prospect in this batch whose income fails the test while everything else fits, which is the pattern the ICP file's own third observation predicts. Second, the ICP again has nothing to say about a chronic lower back under monthly clinical care, which is the most material fact about this prospect.
